payload.author: coordinator
evidence: Local compiler CRT/SRC/HEAPINIT.C declares HANDLE _crtheap and constructs it via HeapCreate; the original code at 0x647D7A stores that return in 0x9C11C4 and uses HeapDestroy on small-block initialization failure. CRT/SRC/SBHEAP.C and WINHEAP.H identify the header-list/scan/defer/count/capacity globals; original 0x647DB6 allocates 0x140 bytes and establishes the corresponding state. Pinned heapinit.obj and sbheap.obj express these globals as COFF common allocation requests, while the fresh map labels their candidate addresses <common>. Native link-code correspondence cannot prove common selection or object size from that label. No replacement C++ global or operand-derived alias should be introduced.
payload.hypothesis: The ledger allocator depends on CRT-owned common globals, not missing application definitions. Use the local CRT sources as provenance-bearing hints, map the original heap initialization path, and require complete current link-input/common-selection evidence before admitting those globals or exporting library targets. A public map address and a four-byte common request alone do not prove the selected allocation extent.
